top_choice_rationale: P001 is a prediction of a new symmetry-protected phase (the time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulator with helical edge channels) followed by a decisive experiment, quantised edge conductance in HgTe/CdTe wells, with nearly two decades of independent confirmation and a stable interpretation. The three names cover distinct, non-substitutable steps (Kane and Mele the theory, Molenkamp the experiment) and a citation restricted to the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall effect keeps the claim bounded; the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is a limit of a three-name prize, not an error in the physics, and the 2016 prize did not cover time-reversal-invariant insulators. P002 (optical lattice clocks) is a mature, cleanly credited two-name invention and realisation and is my second choice, ahead of P003, whose exact fluctuation relations are sound but whose credit set omits a decisive contributor (Crooks or Searles). Any award I find acceptable ranks above no award.
recusal_note: No conflict with Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Katori, Ye, Jarzynski, Evans or Seifert is apparent from my profile. My own field (circuit QED, B042) is not in this slate; Chalmers colleagues and WACQT links relate only to the 2025 prize area, not to these proposals.
